_comment: Settings for the 2028 cycle. Values marked FROM REPLICATION come from the authors' replication files (Enns et al., doi:10.7910/DVN/PBGFOF); values marked ASSUMPTION are this site's own.

election._dates_note: Data cutoff is forecast_day (100 days before the election): only polls conducted by then count, judged by field dates, so a poll conducted in time but published later still counts. The forecast publishes a week later, on publish_day, so most late-published polls are in.

candidates._comment: Nominees, running mates and their home states are detected automatically (pipeline/candidates.py). Fill any of the four *_home fields only to override detection. home_lag = the previous election's nominees (2024: Harris CA, Trump FL).
candidates._home_lag_weight_note: Share of the previous nominees' home-state fade that is applied. 1 = the model as fitted. The site used 0.5 until the replication files arrived; the refit on 1980-2024 (docs/engine.js) now learns the fade from the 2024 results (-3.07, down from -3.49), so halving it as well would count that evidence twice.
candidates._primary_note: Possible candidates in the ticket picker are ordered by their average in national 2028 primary polls (PollResults.org) over the last primary_window_days. Anyone at primary_min_pct or more who is not in candidates.json is added automatically.

vp_adjustment._comment: auto: applied when the sitting vice president (read from Wikipedia) is a nominee. Uses VoteHub job-approval polls of the vice president (VP net minus president net), or favorability if there are none in the window. Set mode to manual and fill vp_net/president_net to override.
vp_adjustment._full_weight_note: ASSUMPTION, not in the paper: the gap is scaled by (polls of the vice president / full_weight_polls), capped at 1, so a handful of polls cannot swing the result. Set to 0 to always use the full gap.

economy._delta_note: FROM REPLICATION: 0.55, the median fitted weight for 2008-2016, simulated from 0.52 to 0.58 in steps of 0.01 (Figures1andA2_2024.do). One model fit per value; docs/engine.js holds the fits in this order.
economy._signed_note: FROM REPLICATION: economic growth is multiplied by -1 under a Republican president (Figures1andA2_2024.do).

approval._constant_note: FROM REPLICATION (inferred): the authors' data stores approval already centered, and the center is 44. Their approval surveys average 44.2% approve (ReadMe), the centered variable moves by whole points between forecast years, and comparing it with national approval in each election from 1980 to 2024 gives 43.6 +/- 0.6.
approval._pollresults_note: PollResults.org (NYT poll data, CC BY 4.0, non-commercial). Merged into the national average; its state polls feed state_source state_polls. If its format changes, the run logs a warning and continues with VoteHub only.
approval._state_source_note: csv (used): state differences come from a copy of Civiqs's public Trump approval tracker kept in pipeline/state_approval.csv (columns state,approve), dated by state_csv_as_of; the differences between states are kept and re-centered on the national poll average. state_live_read: false = no daily request to Civiqs. Its site answers automatic reads with HTTP 403, so the copy stays fixed until Civiqs agrees to regular access; set true only then (pipeline/civiqs.py does the read). Other options: state_polls: vote_swing, pulled toward any state approval polls from the window plus 60 days. vote_swing: state = national + k * (Trump 2024 two-party share in state - national).

head_to_head._comment: Second model: DeSart (2025), doi:10.1017/S1049096524000805. National head-to-head general-election polls between one named Democrat and one named Republican, from PollResults.org.
head_to_head._cannot_run_note: Two-term presidents cannot be nominees (22nd Amendment), so matchups naming them are left out. The sitting president is added automatically.
head_to_head._window_note: DEPARTURE: DeSart uses polls from October of the year before the election (October 2027). The Nowcast uses the last window_days days instead.
head_to_head._min_polls_note: A chosen nominee or pairing needs at least this many polls to be judged on its own polls; otherwise a wider set is used.

ensemble._comment: The Nowcast is the plain average of the approval and economy model and the polls model, state by state (docs/combine.js). No third model. Method frozen 2026-11-12.
